label: Game A
nuance_found: Stacking three different layers (lettuce, tomato, cheese) on one tower makes a CLUB with +25% everything, so spreading upgrades across a few towers beats maxing one. Also the active buttons: Flame on a burner roasted a whole lane of olives, Rinse pushed a lane back, Pepper sneezes. Knights shrug off toothpicks and brutes eat 3 bites, so the tower mix and where you build matter by stage 3-4.
audio: Music loops on the build screens and a victory jingle; thwip, pop, cannon and splurt sounds with a wave ding. Music drops out during some wave stretches but the effects never stop.
furthest_progress: Beat stages 1 (Cutting Board, 3 stars), 2 (Stovetop incl. The Jar boss, 3 stars) and 3 (Sink, 2 stars); lost stage 4 (Sunday Lunch) on wave 8 of 12 at about 543 s when brutes ate the sandwich
control_trouble: Tower-pad taps in the Sink stage often did nothing until I used a longer 150 ms press; the cause could be the harness. Otherwise none.
best_moment: Fourth-layer CLUB popup and the combo x33 chains, and watching the jar boss lose its lid then get roasted.
worst_moment: First stage is slow: about 15 s of walking olives before anything happens, and stage 4 brutes ate the sandwich in a few seconds with no obvious way to react.
verdict: Honestly this is a proper tower defence, closer to Bloons than Candy Crush, but it is the kind of thing I would play on the bus. Clear goal straight away: stop the olives eating the sandwich. Money comes in with every pop, the numbers and combo text pop, and each stage looks different (counter, hob, sink, dinner table) with a new enemy that makes you rethink. The first minute is a bit of a wait, and I mostly watched in the early waves. Stage 4 got hard quickly and I lost to brutes. I would keep it and try again this week.
